rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked every pronoun/demonstrative in all 5 chunks against prior-chunk history. Chunk 1: "all three of these" (line 5) resolves within the same sentence to the colon-list that follows; "Each leg" (line 5) and "The legs" (line 7) both anchor to that same-sentence enumeration. Chunk 2: "it" x2 (line 12) = the instruction channel just named; "They" (line 13) = the attacker; "That sentence" / "this move" (line 13) = the sentence/move just described. Chunk 3: "This" (line 17, "This asks who attacks the agent") contrasts with "Classic threat modeling asks..." in the same sentence and resolves against the trifecta frame named in chunk 1 ("Simon Willison's frame") plus this chunk's own header — holdable under a sequential deck read. "The two audits" (line 18) is cataphoric, resolved by the immediately following clause naming both. Chunk 4: "one" / "a leg" (line 23) = the three legs established in chunk 1; "untrusted input" (line 25) = "untrusted content" from chunk 1, same concept. No never-named, vague-with-full-history, or re-chunk-stranded referents found.

Chunk 3 line 18, "the access-surface map and the STRIDE pass you ran on the feature," names the activity by content/claim, not by file position — the maintainer block itself documents this was de-sequenced from "The surface map and STRIDE from M3" specifically to avoid a positional callback. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess/predict-before-reveal construction anywhere in the file; this is a reference/frame page, not a live-demo beat.

All 5 chunks carry a self-carrying, multi-bullet claim; none is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet. Chunk 4's closing kicker ("Three legs. Cut one.") sits inside a chunk with three full bullets of substantive content, not standalone.

Chunk 1 "Three capabilities that must not meet" -> content lists the three (private data, untrusted content, outbound channel) and explains why their combination leaks. Chunk 2 "An LLM can't reliably tell instructions from data" -> content is exactly that mechanism plus the prompt-injection consequence. Chunk 3 "The attacker targets the agent, not the system" -> content contrasts classic threat modeling with the agent-as-target frame. Chunk 4 "Removing any one leg breaks the trifecta" -> content is the audit-and-cut procedure plus Willison's constraint rule. No header contradicted by its own chunk.

Checked all six sub-items across all 5 chunks. "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction: chunk 1 line 6 "Not risky. Structural." carries only one "Not" clause, not the banned two-"Not"-then-assertion triple. Anaphora/epistrophe triples: chunk 4 line 24's four-clause mitigation list ("Read-only where write is not needed. No network where network is not needed. Allowlisted domains where the web is needed. A human gate...") varies subject and partially varies the closing predicate across four DIFFERENT concrete techniques, not a repeated-subject/repeated-ending rhetorical triple with an empty third leg. Self-grading superlatives: none found. Number + own retraction: none found (the ~95%-detection figure from the source is deliberately kept out per the maintainer's source-verification note, so no number-with-hedge pattern appears at all). Abstraction-noun stacks: none found ("context window," "exploit chain," "instruction channel" are concrete technical terms, not maintainer-abstraction stacks). Verb triplets with an empty leg: none found.
